# Drákōn, translated into industries: what the archetype actually does
Archetypes are not metaphors; they are job descriptions written early. **Drákōn**'s was unusually clear.

Every Greek dragon is a threshold made flesh: kill one and a sanctuary, a city, or a marriage becomes possible — which is why the founders of cities are all, sooner or later, dragonslayers.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Drákōn
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Domain of influence:** Serpent, Guardian, Vigilance
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Technology & Innovation · Culture & Entertainment · Commerce & Governance · Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Cybersecurity & Digital Protection
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 70 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**Apóllōn and Python.** The Homeric Hymn to Apóllōn tells how the god, seeking a site for his oracle, found the spring at Delphoi guarded by a great she-dragon who had nursed Typhaon and ravaged the flocks.  He shot her and left her to rot in the sun — "now rot (pytheu) here upon the fruitful soil" — and the place was called Pythō, the priestess Pythia, ever after. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**Kadmos at the Spring.** Sent to fetch water from the Ismenian spring, Kadmos' companions were killed by its guardian dragon, offspring of Árēs.  Kadmos crushed it with a rock, and on Athēnā's counsel sowed half its teeth: armed men, the Spartoi, rose from the furrows and killed each other until five remained — the ancestors of Thebes' noble houses. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Cybersecurity & Digital Protection

*Threat defense, authentication, and digital trust. (Sector: Technology & Innovation)*

*The unsleeping watcher at the perimeter; the guardian serpent of every firewall.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Drákōn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP

*Video games, streaming franchises, and fantasy worlds. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*Every fantasy dragon is his descendant, hoard and coil included.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Insurance & Protection Services

*Insurance, assurance, and risk protection. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*His coil is the guarding embrace around the treasure; asset protection is his posture.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Drákōn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Freshwater & Hydrology

*Water supply, irrigation, and watershed management. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The dragon at the spring is myth's watermark; he guards the source every utility taps.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Every Greek dragon is a threshold made flesh: kill one and a sanctuary, a city, or a marriage becomes possible — which is why the founders of cities are all, sooner or later, dragonslayers. The age changed. The work did not.

If you work in cybersecurity & digital protection, gaming, fantasy & entertainment ip, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/drakon/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
